html:
SMTO-SSH-0007 — SSH details were too large for SMTO to check

GUID: 917a1127-afe3-4489-86a4-320aac9d5990
Slug: ssh-evidence-limit
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: ssh

What happened

  • To remember a computer, SMTO reads SSH's connection record and the list of trusted computers. One of them was too large (over 256 KB), or this conversation had too many saved connections to that computer, so SMTO didn't save it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your command already did its job on the remote computer before running it again. SMTO reads these files after the command finishes, so the command may have completed.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer whether its trusted-computers file (~/.ssh/known_hosts) is over 256 KB, and to remove entries for computers that no longer exist. SMTO won't read a trusted-computers file larger than 256 KB, so it can't confirm the key stored there.
  3. If you connected to this computer many times with different accounts or settings in this conversation, continue in a new conversation by typing /new. SMTO handles at most eight saved connections to the same computer in one conversation.

What success looks like

  • The next SSH command to that computer runs without this message, and later commands reuse the connection.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete the whole trusted-computers file to make it smaller; keep the entry for this computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A size-limited SSH evidence read (the handshake log or the known_hosts file) exceeded 262,144 bytes or was not a regular file, or a continuity request listed more than eight known setups.

What this means

  • A bounded SSH evidence read exceeds its byte limit or the continuity request supplies a non-list or more than eight known identities. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • A bounded SSH evidence read exceeds its byte limit or the continuity request supplies a non-list or more than eight known identities.

How to diagnose it

  • Separate malformed known-identity input from an oversized captured file.

How to fix it

  • read_bounded in src/gateway_core/ssh_context.py rejects non-regular files and files over MAX_LOG (262144 bytes) for the -E handshake log and the known_hosts file named in 'Found key in'; observe rejects more than eight known setups. Prune stale known_hosts entries (or use a smaller dedicated UserKnownHostsFile) while keeping the target's entry, or re-enroll in a new conversation to reduce matching setups. Do not delete retained receipts to work around the limit.
  • Correct the known-identity list and retain only required supported evidence within the advertised bounds.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The bounded request and evidence validate without truncating away required identity facts.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
